source.title: Training Matching Pursuit SAEs on LLMs

record.tranche_reason: Compares a different SAE architecture with traditional SAEs and measures reconstruction quality, bearing on whether changing architecture reduces reconstruction error. It does not analyze the structure or cause of the error.
record.gate_note: The post reports reconstruction comparisons relevant to V6. Its k-sparse probing and feature-absorption results concern SAE quality but do not measure the dark-matter properties in the claim versions, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The post compares a highly nonlinear matching-pursuit encoder with BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs at matched L0 and width. It reports variance explained, which bears weakly on whether reconstruction error shrinks with a different architecture (V6). No magnitudes are given, and the error itself is never analyzed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. MP-SAEs reconstruct better than traditional SAEs at matched L0. However, they do worse on sparse probing and absorption, are much slower to train, and are not recommended for practical interpretability. The author suspects the reconstruction gains come from degenerate solutions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Matching Pursuit encoders and compares them with BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs; does not perform the original dark-matter analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction results are compared at L0=85 and L0=265; the static L0=85 MP-SAE is reported to reconstruct slightly better than the standard L0=85 MP-SAE.

fits_no_version.finding: MP-SAEs score notably worse on k=1 and k=16 sparse probing and much worse on SAEBench absorption than traditional SAEs, despite better reconstruction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural reductions in SAE reconstruction error can come from degenerate strategies (absorption) rather than from learning more of the model's features.

record.problems: The author describes the investigation as not rigorous and limited to a few MP-SAEs on Gemma-2-2b. The supplied text gives no numerical variance-explained values or uncertainty for the reconstruction comparisons; it does not analyze the error itself.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for BatchTopK reconstruction: the text does not state its result separately beyond the general traditional-SAE comparison. K-sparse probing, feature absorption, training times, decoder norms, and dead-latent observations are omitted because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether dark matter mostly reflects training artifacts. Untested parts: the magnitude of error reduction, effects of the sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents or objective, end-to-end training, and whether the remaining error is model structure.
Not tested: linear predictability of the SAE error.
Not tested: per-token error norms or behaviour of the error across SAE sizes.
Not tested: loss under SAE reconstructions versus random errors.
Not tested: separation of linear and nonlinear error components.
Not tested: circuit or steering analyses with and without the error term.

missing.what: Sparse-probing (k=1, k=16) and absorption results that the author uses to interpret the reconstruction gain as degenerate. They are needed to read the V6 verdict, even though they are not dark-matter measures.
missing.locator: 'MP-SAEs underperform at K-Sparse Probing' and 'very susceptible to feature absorption' sections

missing.what: Actual variance-explained values per SAE, shown only in figures not present in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal, self-described non-rigorous LessWrong post with no numbers in the text and no uncertainty. Its bearing on V6 is indirect: it shows error depends on encoder architecture, but it does not measure dark matter as defined in the original.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether SAE error is linearly predictable from input activations.
No per-token error-norm prediction, comparison of contexts failing across SAE sizes, or test of whether error vanishes with scale.
No comparison of model loss under SAE reconstructions versus random errors of the same size.
No analysis separating linear and nonlinear error components, or testing whether they correspond to unlearned features and resist dictionary learning.
No test of how retaining or dropping SAE error affects circuits, steering, or model behaviour.

Tests whether a different SAE architecture improves reconstruction, but does not establish whether dark matter mostly reflects training artifacts, examine sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents, or objective effects, or test end-to-end training.

relationships.condition: MP-SAEs vs BatchTopK/Matryoshka, Gemma-2-2b layer 12, 32k width, L0=85 and 265, 300M tokens
relationships.reason: Error is lower with a nonlinear MP encoder (r1–r3), but the author attributes this to degenerate absorption, with worse k-sparse probing (text). So lower error need not mean better capture of model features.
relationships.display_finding: The nonlinear matching-pursuit encoder reduced reconstruction error relative to BatchTopK and Matryoshka, but worsened k-sparse probing; the author attributed the improvement to degenerate absorption.

relation.reason: Its own reconstruction comparisons bear on whether changing SAE architecture reduces error, although they do not establish the dominant cause of dark matter.

tranche.reason: Comparing reconstruction under a different encoder provides a limited architecture-sensitivity test relevant to V6, without reproducing the original dark-matter analyses.

source_check.notes: Reconstruction results are qualitative in the supplied text. The author explicitly describes this as an informal investigation and treats degenerate absorption as a possible explanation.

statements.correction: Gemma-2-2b layer 12; width 32k; 300M training tokens; standard MP L0 approximately 85 and 265; static MP L0=85; better reconstruction; worse k=1 and k=16 sparse probing; worse absorption scores; degeneration proposed; reconstruction improvement magnitude unstated; no demonstrated V6 scope limitation.
statements.problem: The experimental facts match, but the limits_scope label does not follow: V6 makes no promise about sparse probing or feature quality. Degenerate absorption is a proposed explanation.
